title: Sprint 1 — Project Setup & Authentication
description: Initialize the Django REST API project, configure Django REST Framework with SQLite, and build secure token-based user registration, login, and logout API endpoints.

tickets.title: TODO-001: Initialize Django REST API Project
tickets.description:
### Overview
Set up the backend development environment for the Django ToDo REST API. Initialize a new Django project named `todoproject` and create a dedicated API application named `tasks`. Install and configure Django REST Framework (DRF) within `INSTALLED_APPS`, configure the default DRF settings and SQLite database in `todoproject/settings.py`, apply initial database migrations, and establish a root API health-check endpoint (`GET /api/health/`) that returns a JSON status response.

### Dependencies
- None (First ticket in the project).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Django project named `todoproject` and application named `tasks` are initialized.
- [ ] `rest_framework` and `tasks` are added to `INSTALLED_APPS` in `todoproject/settings.py`.
- [ ] SQLite database is configured in `DATABASES` and default migrations are applied cleanly via `python manage.py migrate`.
- [ ] Default `REST_FRAMEWORK` settings are defined (including default renderers and parsers for JSON).
- [ ] A health check endpoint `GET /api/health/` responds with HTTP 200 OK and JSON payload `{"status": "ok", "message": "Django ToDo API is running"}`.
- [ ] The development server starts without warnings or errors via `python manage.py runserver`.

### Expected Deliverables
- `manage.py`
- `todoproject/settings.py`
- `todoproject/urls.py`
- `tasks/apps.py`
- `tasks/views.py` with health check endpoint
- Initial database file `db.sqlite3`

### Evaluation Criteria
- Verification that DRF is registered in `INSTALLED_APPS`.
- `GET /api/health/` returns HTTP 200 with `application/json` content type.
- Database migrations execute without errors.
learning_objectives: Understand Django REST Framework project architecture.
Configure settings.py for DRF, SQLite, and JSON rendering.
Build a basic RESTful API endpoint using DRF APIView or @api_view.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Project and App Setup
tasks.description: Initialize the Django project `todoproject` and create the `tasks` app. Register `'rest_framework'` and `'tasks'` in `INSTALLED_APPS` inside `todoproject/settings.py`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Database and DRF Configuration
tasks.description: Configure SQLite in `DATABASES`. Add `REST_FRAMEWORK` dictionary to `settings.py` with default JSON renderers and parsers. Run `python manage.py migrate`.

tasks.title: Task 3 — Health Check API Endpoint
tasks.description: Implement a `health_check` endpoint using DRF `@api_view(['GET'])` returning `Response({'status': 'ok', 'message': 'Django ToDo API is running'}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)`. Map it to `/api/health/`.

common_mistakes: Returning a plain Django HttpResponse or string instead of a DRF Response object with JSON data.
Skipping database migrations before running the server.
hints: Use `from rest_framework.decorators import api_view` and `from rest_framework.response import Response`.

tickets.title: TODO-002: Implement User Registration API
tickets.description:
### Overview
Build a public REST API endpoint that allows new users to register an account by submitting JSON payloads. Create a DRF `Serializer` that validates incoming registration fields: `username`, `email`, and `password`. The serializer must ensure the username is unique, validate email format, enforce password strength, and create the user using `User.objects.create_user()` to ensure the password is securely hashed. The API response must return the created user details with HTTP 201 Created and must NEVER expose the raw password or password hash.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-001`: Initialize Django REST API Project.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint `POST /api/auth/register/` is configured and accepts JSON requests.
- [ ] Accepts JSON body containing `username`, `email`, and `password`.
- [ ] Serializer validates that `username` and `password` are present and non-empty.
- [ ] Duplicate usernames return HTTP 400 Bad Request with descriptive validation error messages.
- [ ] Invalid email formats return HTTP 400 Bad Request.
- [ ] Passwords are saved using `create_user()` with PBKDF2/Argon2 hashing; passwords are never stored in plain text.
- [ ] Successful registration returns HTTP 201 Created with JSON body containing user ID, username, and email (e.g. `{"id": 1, "username": "student1", "email": "student1@example.com"}`).
- [ ] The response payload strictly excludes password, password hash, and secret attributes.

### Expected Deliverables
- `tasks/serializers.py` containing `UserRegistrationSerializer`.
- `tasks/views.py` containing `RegisterAPIView` or registration view.
- Route `POST /api/auth/register/` registered in URL patterns.

### Evaluation Criteria
- `POST /api/auth/register/` with valid payload returns HTTP 201 Created.
- Verification of user record in `auth_user` table with hashed password.
- Duplicate registration returns HTTP 400 with `{ "username": [ ... ] }` error structure.
- Response body inspected to confirm password is absent.
learning_objectives: Create DRF Serializers for incoming request payload validation.
Implement secure user creation using Django's User.objects.create_user.
Enforce write-only serializer fields to prevent sensitive data leakage.
Return standard REST HTTP status codes (201 Created, 400 Bad Request).

tasks.title: Task 1 — User Registration Serializer
tasks.description: Create `tasks/serializers.py` and define `UserRegistrationSerializer`. Declare `password` with `write_only=True`. Validate username uniqueness and email format. Implement `create(self, validated_data)` using `User.objects.create_user()`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Registration API View and URL Routing
tasks.description: Create `RegisterView(generics.CreateAPIView)` or `@api_view(['POST'])` in `tasks/views.py`. Wire endpoint to `/api/auth/register/`. Return HTTP 201 on success or HTTP 400 with serializer errors.

common_mistakes: Using User.objects.create() instead of create_user(), which stores passwords in plain text.
Returning the password field in the response payload instead of marking it write_only=True.
Returning HTTP 200 OK instead of the REST standard HTTP 201 Created for resource creation.
hints: Test registration with curl or Postman using `Content-Type: application/json`.

solution.views_py:
from rest_framework import generics, permissions
from .serializers import UserRegistrationSerializer

class RegisterView(generics.CreateAPIView):
    serializer_class = UserRegistrationSerializer
    permission_classes = [permissions.AllowAny]

tickets.title: TODO-003: Implement Login and Logout APIs
tickets.description:
### Overview
Implement REST authentication endpoints for login and logout using Django REST Framework. Add `'rest_framework.authtoken'` to `INSTALLED_APPS` and run migrations to create token tables. Build `POST /api/auth/login/` to authenticate username and password credentials; upon success, generate or retrieve a token and return `{"token": "...", "user_id": 1, "username": "..."}` with HTTP 200 OK. Build `POST /api/auth/logout/` requiring an authenticated token in the `Authorization: Token <token>` header; this endpoint deletes the token from the database and returns HTTP 200 OK with `{"message": "Successfully logged out"}`.

### Dependencies
- `TODO-002`: Implement User Registration API.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rest_framework.authtoken` is enabled and migrated in SQLite.
- [ ] `POST /api/auth/login/` accepts JSON with `username` and `password`.
- [ ] Valid credentials return HTTP 200 OK with auth token string, user ID, and username.
- [ ] Invalid credentials return HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 401 Unauthorized with error message `{"error": "Invalid username or password"}`.
- [ ] `POST /api/auth/logout/` requires valid token authentication (`Authorization: Token <key>`).
- [ ] Logout deletes the authentication token record from the database so it can no longer be used.
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests to logout endpoint return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
- [ ] Successful logout returns HTTP 200 OK with `{"message": "Successfully logged out"}`.

### Expected Deliverables
- `todoproject/settings.py` updated with `rest_framework.authtoken`.
- `tasks/views.py` containing `LoginAPIView` and `LogoutAPIView`.
- Routes mapped in `todoproject/urls.py` (`POST /api/auth/login/` and `POST /api/auth/logout/`).

### Evaluation Criteria
- Token verification: Valid login produces a 40-character DRF Token.
- Token invalidation: Calling logout deletes the token; subsequent requests with the old token return HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
- Invalid login attempts return appropriate error status codes.
learning_objectives: Issue and invalidate REST API tokens upon login and logout.
Protect endpoints requiring Authorization: Token <key> headers.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Enable Token Authentication
tasks.description: Add `'rest_framework.authtoken'` to `INSTALLED_APPS` in `settings.py` and run `python manage.py migrate`. Set `DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES` to include `'rest_framework.authentication.TokenAuthentication'`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Login API Endpoint
tasks.description: Create `LoginView` handling `POST /api/auth/login/`. Authenticate credentials using `authenticate(username=..., password=...)`. On success, retrieve or create token with `Token.objects.get_or_create(user=user)` and return token, user_id, and username with HTTP 200. On failure, return HTTP 400/401.

tasks.title: Task 3 — Logout API Endpoint
tasks.description: Create `LogoutView` handling `POST /api/auth/logout/`. Set `permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]`. Delete the requesting user's token using `request.user.auth_token.delete()`. Return `{'message': 'Successfully logged out'}` with HTTP 200.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to run migrations after adding 'rest_framework.authtoken', causing database table missing errors.
Not deleting the token on logout, allowing expired credentials to remain active.
Using GET instead of POST for login and logout operations.
hints: Import `from rest_framework.authtoken.models import Token` and `from django.contrib.auth import authenticate`.
Authenticated requests must send headers in format: `Authorization: Token <token_key>`.
Use `request.user.auth_token.delete()` to invalidate the active token.
